name: relay
title: An outbound relay
summary: A server that sends mail for applications and other servers and holds no mailbox anybody reads. IMAP and POP3 are closed at the next restart, an address that bounces hard is suppressed and a submission to it refused at once, deliveries back off from a destination that asks them to and never hold more than ten sessions open to one, and every message is traced and the trace kept for three months, because a relay is asked about what it sent long after it sent it.
steps: Decide who may relay: that is an IP range's question - require authentication on the range the senders connect from, or name their addresses - and a profile does not answer it.

Turn on "Require SSL/TLS when authenticating" on the IP range the senders connect from, or make the submission port STARTTLS-required: that is what refuses a password sent in the clear, and an IP range is not a setting a profile can write.

Raise [Database] NumberOfConnections in hMailServer.ini to about the delivery thread count, 25 here: the deliveries, the sign-ins and the rest share that pool, five connections as shipped, and a wait for one longer than DBConnectionAcquireTimeout fails.
Switch DKIM signing and its key rotation on for each sending domain: both are the domain's, and the server has no value of them to set.
Set the sending limits per account in [SendingLimits] if the senders are to be held to a volume: those keys are the settings file's, not the store's.

entries.name: protocolimap
entries.why: nobody reads mail on a relay, and a listener nobody uses is one more to attack; it closes at the next restart

entries.name: protocolpop3
entries.why: the same for POP3, which also closes at the next restart

entries.name: AutoBanOnLogonFailureEnabled
entries.why: an address that keeps failing to sign in with a relay's credentials is banned, as shipped

entries.name: CreateDefaultSpecialUseFolders
entries.why: an account created here gets no Drafts, Sent, Junk or Trash, as shipped: it is a sender's credential, not a mailbox

entries.name: DirectoryEnabled
entries.why: the directory, which lists a domain's accounts to one another over REST and CardDAV, is not answered: the accounts are applications, not people

entries.name: BounceProcessingEnabled
entries.why: every bounce is read and counted, and an address that reaches the hard-bounce threshold is suppressed for its sending domain

entries.name: BounceHardBounceThreshold
entries.why: one hard bounce suppresses the address, as shipped: the receiver has refused it permanently

entries.name: BounceSuppressionAction
entries.why: a submission to a suppressed address is refused at RCPT, as shipped, so the application learns it at once rather than from a bounce

entries.name: BounceSuppressionExpiryDays
entries.why: an automatic suppression is removed after six months, giving the address another chance, where none is removed as shipped; one added by hand stays

entries.name: BounceReadDeliveryReports
entries.why: a delivery report that arrives later counts as a bounce when it names a message this server sent, as shipped

entries.name: OutboundBackoffMaxMinutes
entries.why: a destination that keeps asking this server to slow down is left alone for at most an hour at a time, as shipped

entries.name: OutboundBackoffMinutes
entries.why: a destination that answers a slow-down reply is left alone for two minutes, doubling while it keeps asking, as shipped

entries.name: MaxOutboundConnsPerDestination
entries.why: no destination is held more than ten sessions from this server at once, where the delivery threads are the only limit as shipped

entries.name: maxdelivertythreads
entries.why: twenty-five deliveries run at once rather than the ten shipped, because a relay's work is delivery

entries.name: smtpnoofretries
entries.why: twelve retries rather than the four shipped, so a destination that is down for most of a working day still gets its mail

entries.name: smtpminutesbetweenretries
entries.why: an hour between the retries after the quick ones, as shipped

entries.name: QuickRetries
entries.why: the first two retries come QuickRetriesMinutes apart, six minutes as shipped, for a receiver that greylists or failed for a moment

entries.name: SmtpDeliveryConnectionSecurity
entries.why: a delivery to a recipient's MX host uses STARTTLS whenever the host offers it, as shipped

entries.name: VerifyRemoteSslCertificate
entries.why: the certificate of a host this server delivers to is verified, as shipped: a failure ends a connection that requires TLS, and is forgiven on an opportunistic STARTTLS

entries.name: MtaStsEnabled
entries.why: a recipient domain whose MTA-STS policy is in enforce mode is delivered to only over TLS to a host its policy names, as shipped

entries.name: DaneEnforcementEnabled
entries.why: a recipient MX host with DNSSEC-signed TLSA records is held to them, as shipped

entries.name: MessageTraceEnabled
entries.why: each message's acceptance, refusal, delivery and failure is recorded by queue id, which answers what happened to it; it is a record of who writes to whom

entries.name: MessageTraceRetentionDays
entries.why: three months of the trace rather than the thirty days shipped, because a relay is asked about old sends

entries.name: ReputationWatchEnabled
entries.why: once a day the addresses this server knows it sends from are looked up in the block lists receivers use, and a listing is reported, as shipped
